title: CI/CD rollback breadcrumbs - canary failure notes
content:
Summary:
- Quick personal scratchpad capturing commands, outputs, and hypotheses from the canary failure on 2026-02-26 (canary id: canary-2026-02-26-a).
- Objective: preserve breadcrumbs so SRE and release team can reproduce rollback steps and audit decisions.

Timeline (short):
- 2026-02-26 09:12 UTC: Canary rollout started (helm chart v1.9.2 -> v1.10.0) using release 'platform-api-canary' in namespace 'platform-staging'.
- 2026-02-26 09:19 UTC: Automated canary metrics tripped (error rate spike in /v1/generate endpoint).
- 2026-02-26 09:21 UTC: Paused rollout, escalated to on-call. Began troubleshooting.
- 2026-02-26 09:35 UTC: Decided to rollback to previous chart revision (v1.9.2).

Commands tried (exact):
1) Check current helm history and status:
   helm --kube-context=staging -n platform-staging history platform-api-canary --max=10
   Output:
   REVISION	UPDATED                  	STATUS	CHART	APP VERSION	DESCRIPTION
   4	2026-02-26 09:12:11	DEPLOYED	platform-api-1.10.0	1.10.0	Deployed revision 4
   3	2026-02-23 02:11:03	SUPERSEDED	platform-api-1.9.2	1.9.2	Rolled back to 3

2) Attempted helm rollback to revision 3:
   helm --kube-context=staging -n platform-staging rollback platform-api-canary 3
   Output:
   Rollback was a success for release: platform-api-canary

3) Verify pods restarted and image digests:
   kubectl --context=staging -n platform-staging get pods -l app=platform-api -o wide
   kubectl --context=staging -n platform-staging describe pod platform-api-canary-5d77f9c6b9-abcde
   kubectl --context=staging -n platform-staging get rs -l app=platform-api -o yaml | grep image:
   Output snippet: image: ghcr.io/redwood-inference/platform-api@sha256:abcd1234ef5678...

4) Check logs for failing pod (post-rollback):
   kubectl --context=staging -n platform-staging logs platform-api-canary-5d77f9c6b9-abcde -c platform-api | tail -n 200
   Error seen before rollback (from revision 4 pods):
   2026-02-26T09:18:51Z ERROR http: handler failed: panic: runtime error: index out of range
   stacktrace:
     runtime.go:45 main.(*handler).Serve(handlers.go:123)

5) Query metrics from Prometheus (canary window):
   curl -s "https://prometheus.redwood.internal/api/v1/query_range?query=rate(http_requests_total{route=\"/v1/generate\",job=\"platform-api\"}[1m])&start=1708912800&end=1708912960&step=15" | jq .data
   Observed: error_rate increased from 0.3% -> 8.5% over 8 minutes, p95 latency jumped from 210ms -> 1.9s.

Observed outputs / weirdness:
- Helm reported rollback success, but one replica stayed in CrashLoopBackOff for ~4 minutes after rollback.
- Crash stacktrace points to index-bound panic in tokenization code path introduced in model-adapter v0.12. The release included model-adapter v0.12.1 compiled into platform-api image.
- Image digest for revision 4: sha256:deadbeef... (v1.10.0). Revision 3 referenced sha256:abcd1234... (v1.9.2).
- There is a discrepancy between the docker tag and chart version in artifact registry for v1.10.0; the image tagged 'v1.10.0' points to digest deadbeef but there's an additional 'v1.10.0-hotfix' digest differ. Need to reconcile publishing pipeline outputs.

Hypotheses:
1) Code/regression: model-adapter v0.12.1 introduced a boundary check regression that only surfaces for certain sequence lengths seen in production traffic -> causes panic. Explains index out of range and spike in error rate.
2) Canary traffic routing: Some traffic still hitting revision 4 pods due to old replicaset leftovers or sticky connections at the ALB layer. Explains delay in full traffic shift even after helm rollback.
3) Artifact mismatch: Image tag vs digest mismatch (publish race) caused an unintended binary to be included in chart revision 4. Release pipeline may have pushed image then updated chart with wrong digest.
4) Config / feature flag: New config defaults enabled in v1.10.0 (eg TOKEN_SEGMENTATION_STRICT=true) causing different code path.

Immediate actions taken (notes):
- Rolled back helm release to revision 3 (confirmed by helm history + deployment replicaset pointing to v1.9.2 digest).
- Scaled down revision 4 replica set to 0 to accelerate draining: kubectl --context=staging -n platform-staging scale rs platform-api-4 --replicas=0 (manual step).
- Opened PROJ-4587 and assigned to @diego (on-call) to triage model-adapter change set.
- Patched canary runbook with step to check image digests between chart and registry before promoting.

Troubleshooting notes / commands to reproduce locally (dev machine):
- Pull both images locally and run quick smoke tests (tokenization paths):
  docker pull ghcr.io/redwood-inference/platform-api@sha256:abcd1234ef5678
  docker run --rm -it ghcr.io/redwood-inference/platform-api@sha256:abcd1234ef5678 /bin/bash
  ./smoke/tokenization_test --seq-len 4096 --model small
- Run unit that reproduces crash: tests/tokenization_test.go::TestBoundaryConditions (suspected flake introduced in v0.12.1).

Failure snippets captured:
- Pod log (revision 4):
  2026-02-26T09:18:51Z ERROR http: handler failed: panic: runtime error: index out of range
  goroutine 12345 [running]:
  github.com/redwood-inference/model-adapter/tokenizer.(*Tokenizer).Encode(
      /workspace/model-adapter/tokenizer/tokenizer.go:212 +0x34f
  )

- Healthcheck errors from ALB: 502 from target /healthz for target ip 10.12.7.45

Open questions / unknowns to follow up:
- Confirm whether the CI image publishing step can race with chart packaging (check release pipeline logs around 2026-02-26 08:55-09:05 UTC). Linked logs: https://ci.internal.redwood/jobs/4521
- Did any configmap updates accompany the chart bump? Check git history for helm values for platform-api env vars.
- Was there any manual intervention in the deploy pipeline (ad-hoc image tag override)?

Next steps / TODOs:
- [ ] Diego: Triage model-adapter PRs that landed between v0.11.x -> v0.12.1; run the boundary tests locally (assigned).
- [ ] Ops: Add a pre-promote validation: ensure image digest referenced in chart matches registry digest for tag. (short-term fix)
- [ ] Release: Add explicit canary abort if error rate > 2% for 5m AND rolling restart hasn't converged.
- [ ] Engineering: Add a fuzz test for tokenizer boundary conditions around seq lengths 512, 1024, 4096.

Notes for post-incident writeup:
- Prepare timeline with timestamps, include crash logs, helm history, image digests, and Prometheus graphs.
- Recommend blocking v1.10.0 until model-adapter regression verified.
- Consider backport hotfix to v1.9.3 if fix trivial and low risk.

References / quick links:
- GH PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/2123
- JIRA: PROJ-4587
- CI job logs: https://ci.internal.redwood/jobs/4521
- Runbook: confluence:Platform/CANARY-Runbook

Random notes / misc (scratch):
- I should capture the full kubectl describe of the crashing pod and attach to the Jira ticket.
- Check ALB sticky session timeout that might keep connections to old pod IPs for ~60s.
- If we see image tag mismatches again, consider moving to digest-only references in canaries.

End of scratchpad.
